recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is +17.3% above baseline (79.9 vs 68.1 ms), but resting HR dropped -7.3% (46.2 vs 49.9 bpm) — a sign of parasympathetic dominance *without* corresponding recovery capacity
Sleep is critically low: 4.9h avg (vs 4.6h baseline), and 14/14 nights <7h — chronic sleep debt
Training readiness latest is only 25 (7d avg = 41.8), well below functional threshold
Recovery balance is +3.18 — unusually high due to suppressed acute load, not robust recovery; reflects undertraining, not resilience
ACWR = 1.0 is optimal on paper, but acute load (209) is 30% below 4-week average (293–638), indicating recent load reduction due to fatigue or disengagement
readiness.guidance: This is not a 'go harder' moment — it's a signal to consolidate, protect sleep, and rebuild autonomic resilience before adding stimulus.

monthly_review.summary: August shows reduced volume and slower pace versus July, with lower aerobic TE and cadence — consistent with intentional recovery or emerging fatigue; the pattern holds across prior months, confirming a deliberate downshift rather than a blip.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +31 spm from July (118 → 149), reversing a multi-month decline — likely reflecting reduced fatigue or conscious form focus, but occurring alongside slower pace and lower efficiency, suggesting compensatory mechanics rather than true economy gain.

goal_tracker.message: Catching up would require ~31.1 km across up to 4 sessions in 2 days — physically impossible and medically inadvisable given compromised readiness, chronic sleep debt (<7h for 14/14 days), and low training readiness (25). Chasing last month’s volume contradicts all recovery metrics and risks injury or burnout.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with worsening running economy
insights.body: Sleep averaged 4.9h (14/14 nights <7h), while running economy (ml O2/kg/km) worsened from 13.64 (Jul) to 14.12 (Aug) — and the latest single-run value is 253.5, the highest in the recent series. Sleep loss impairs neuromuscular coordination and metabolic efficiency, directly elevating oxygen cost.

insights.title: High recovery balance (+3.18) masks under-recovery, not over-recovery
insights.body: Recovery balance is elevated because acute load (209) collapsed — not because HRV or sleep improved sustainably. HRV is up, but resting HR dropped sharply (-3.7 bpm) and sleep remains pathologically low, indicating autonomic fragility masked by low output.

insights.title: Improved decoupling despite slower pace suggests preserved aerobic integrity
insights.body: Latest aerobic decoupling is 4.8% — just under the 5% threshold — even though pace slowed significantly (8:54 vs 8:38) and efficiency declined. This indicates the aerobic system is still holding up, likely due to maintained VO2max (40.0, +4.8% vs baseline) and stable HRV.

insights.title: Cadence surge coincides with longer stride and higher vertical oscillation
insights.body: Cadence rose to 149 spm (Aug) from 118 (Jul), yet stride length increased (e.g., 94.09 cm on 2026-08-27) and vertical oscillation stayed elevated (7.5–8.0 cm). This suggests inefficient 'bouncing' rather than economical turnover — consistent with fatigue compensation or form drift under low readiness.

recommendations.action: Complete two 30-minute Zone 1 walks (HR <115 bpm) on 2026-08-29 and 2026-08-30 — no running, no tracking targets, just movement and breath.
recommendations.reason: To support parasympathetic re-engagement without cardiovascular or musculoskeletal stress, aligning with low training readiness (25) and chronic sleep debt.

recommendations.action: Prioritize sleep hygiene: lights out by 22:00, zero screens after 21:30, and aim for ≥6.5 hours — track via Garmin sleep score, not just duration.
recommendations.reason: Sleep is the strongest lever for restoring HRV stability and lowering oxygen cost; current 4.9h avg is incompatible with sustainable training adaptation.

recommendations.action: Perform daily 5-minute HRV-guided breathing (4-7-8 pattern) using Garmin Body Battery or HRV status as feedback — stop if HRV drops below 70 ms.
recommendations.reason: To reinforce vagal tone amid low resting HR and high HRV variability — preventing further autonomic dysregulation before reintroducing load.

risk_flags.risk: Chronic sleep deprivation increasing injury susceptibility
risk_flags.evidence: 14/14 nights <7h sleep, correlated with elevated vertical oscillation (7.5–8.0 cm) and ground contact time variability (283–385 ms)
risk_flags.action: Immediate sleep-first protocol — no running until ≥6.5h avg achieved for 3 consecutive nights

risk_flags.risk: Autonomic instability masked by low training load
risk_flags.evidence: Resting HR dropped -7.3% (46.2 vs 49.9 bpm) while HRV is elevated (+17.3%), and training readiness is critically low (25)
risk_flags.action: Suspend all HR-zone-based training until resting HR stabilizes between 47–49 bpm and 7d training readiness avg ≥50

weekly_focus.description: Reset nervous system regulation through non-running movement, sleep restoration, and breathwork — prioritizing HRV sustainability over pace, distance, or zone adherence.
